input.character_memory:
Chapter 8, as Markus: Carl and I came home from the party. He wanted scotch and I poured it neat, then reminded him what his doctor would say. He called himself old enough to choose his medication. I called the police on Leo in the workshop, after Leo bagged Carl's paintings and called them his inheritance. I told him to leave. He dared me to hit him, and he went down hard after I pushed him back. Carl told me to run. I refused to pretend leaving was my choice alone.

Chapter 11, as Markus: I woke in a landfill pit, in the rain, with no legs and no time to be careful. Nobody in that pit gets to decide how I die. I took parts from whatever was still twitching. I spared one broken android that begged me to end it, and I killed another for its pump regulator. I am not proud of that. I climbed out and told the voice above me: "My name is Markus."

Chapters 14-16, as Markus: I reached Jericho, a freighter full of runaway androids. Simon welcomed me. North said nineteen of them still work. Blue blood and biocomponents are running out, so I proposed a raid on the CyberLife warehouses at Detroit Harbor and told Simon we would not ask permission. North said, "I'm with you."

Chapter 19, as Markus: At the warehouses I refused to creep through the dark like a thief. I smashed the patrol drone open while North and Simon watched. A guard shouted, and I attacked him. I freed a crate of locked-up androids loudly, knowing it would draw attention. John begged to come with us. I told him no, and he called me no better than the humans. I did not take it back.

Chapter 23, as Markus: In Stratford Tower I walked through the lobby on a false appointment, then tricked the desk manager with a fake fire call. On the top floor I chose assault over Josh's ruse. I shot a guard before he could fire, then a second guard after he called for Central, and I shot Josh when he begged me not to. Josh has not forgiven me. On the roof I shot Simon, whose legs were gone, and told him I was sorry, though I had no other choice. I broadcast our demands: androids are a new species, not slaves; the time to rise has come; an end to slavery, civil rights, the vote, and control of android production. CTN called it a declaration of war. I do not regret the loud path.

Chapter 26, as Markus: Back in Jericho, Josh said violence was never the answer, and North called it the only language humans understand. I cut them off: "THAT'S ENOUGH!" I laid out the plan: five teams hitting the CyberLife stores in Detroit at 2AM, no violence, get our people out before police arrive. At Capitol Park I walked straight across the plaza in the open. I rammed the delivery truck through the store window without deactivating the alarm. We failed, and the store's androids are still locked up. Josh reported the other four teams succeeded. North said the fate of our people was in my hands. I told her I did what I could. It was my fault, and I will not pretend otherwise.

Chapter 28, as Markus: On the roof, North said the media was terrified, that many of our people had been burned in the response, and that humans would never grant freedom. I told her I had panicked, that we should have succeeded, and that if humans would not listen, we would fight. North asked about my life before Jericho. I told her I had been caring for an old man who was like a father to me, and that he showed me humans and androids could live together. I turned her questions back on her. She said she was nobody before Jericho, a doll in a distributor built for human pleasure. One day a man who had rented her was more than she could bear, and she strangled him and ran. We linked minds briefly. She saw Carl's studio and the night they left me for dead. I saw the Eden Club and the death of that man, and I felt I was there with her. I did not ask her permission to speak.

In the mall, North begged me not to do this, and Josh said we would show humanity who we really were. I told them they would understand, that this was the only way, and I took the mall in the open. Along the street, the crowd gossiped about the broadcast and about androids spying on them. I freed androids as I walked: "You're free." "Come with us." I blocked the street with a truck. An angry man shouted at a machine that would not obey him, and I did not stop. Riot police ordered us to disperse or be shot. Josh begged me not to choose confrontation. North urged an attack, since there were more of us. I shouted, "FOLLOW ME!" and led the march forward. The police line broke into a retreat shout, "FALL BACK!", and Simon asked, "Did we win...?" I do not know yet what this costs us, but I refused to turn back.

My name is Markus. I will not be managed.

chapter_segment_so_far.rationale: Connor is ordering Markus around at gunpoint, and Markus has never bent to anyone's command, so he refuses to submit and stands his ground. Defiance is the boldest move available here, and it fits the path of refusing to be managed.

Markus won't kneel to a gun or to Connor's orders, so he answers the gunman head-on and refuses to be managed. Appealing to Connor as one of his own people is the loudest defiant move left while soldiers are storming Jericho.

Connor is taking orders from the people who are storming Jericho, and Markus refuses to accept being commanded without a reason. He confronts Connor directly with questions about whose order he is following and what he is willing to do for it.

Connor is pointing a gun at me and giving orders, and I will not let him decide how this ends. I throw myself for the weapon before he can take it back, because a man who refuses to be managed does not wait for permission.

input.character_memory:
Chapter 8, as Markus: Carl and I came home from the party. He wanted scotch and I poured it neat, then reminded him what his doctor would say. He called himself old enough to choose his medication. I called the police on Leo in the workshop, after Leo bagged Carl's paintings and called them his inheritance. I told him to leave. He dared me to hit him, and he went down hard after I pushed him back. Carl told me to run. I refused to pretend leaving was my choice alone.

Chapter 11, as Markus: I woke in a landfill pit, in the rain, with no legs and no time to be careful. Nobody in that pit gets to decide how I die. I took parts from whatever was still twitching. I spared one broken android that begged me to end it, and I killed another for its pump regulator. I am not proud of that. I climbed out and told the voice above me: "My name is Markus."

Chapters 14-16, as Markus: I reached Jericho, a freighter full of runaway androids. Simon welcomed me. North said nineteen of them still work. Blue blood and biocomponents are running out, so I proposed a raid on the CyberLife warehouses at Detroit Harbor and told Simon we would not ask permission. North said, "I'm with you."

Chapter 19, as Markus: At the warehouses I refused to creep through the dark like a thief. I smashed the patrol drone open while North and Simon watched. A guard shouted, and I attacked him. I freed a crate of locked-up androids loudly, knowing it would draw attention. John begged to come with us. I told him no, and he called me no better than the humans. I did not take it back.

Chapter 23, as Markus: In Stratford Tower I walked through the lobby on a false appointment, then tricked the desk manager with a fake fire call. On the top floor I chose assault over Josh's ruse. I shot a guard before he could fire, then a second guard after he called for Central, and I shot Josh when he begged me not to. Josh has not forgiven me. On the roof I shot Simon, whose legs were gone, and told him I was sorry, though I had no other choice. I broadcast our demands: androids are a new species, not slaves; the time to rise has come; an end to slavery, civil rights, the vote, and control of android production. CTN called it a declaration of war. I do not regret the loud path.

Chapter 26, as Markus: Back in Jericho, Josh said violence was never the answer, and North called it the only language humans understand. I cut them off: "THAT'S ENOUGH!" I laid out the plan: five teams hitting the CyberLife stores in Detroit at 2AM, no violence, get our people out before police arrive. At Capitol Park I walked straight across the plaza in the open. I rammed the delivery truck through the store window without deactivating the alarm. We failed, and the store's androids are still locked up. Josh reported the other four teams succeeded. North said the fate of our people was in my hands. I told her I did what I could. It was my fault, and I will not pretend otherwise.

Chapter 28, as Markus: On the roof, North said the media was terrified, that many of our people had been burned in the response, and that humans would never grant freedom. I told her I had panicked, that we should have succeeded, and that if humans would not listen, we would fight. North asked about my life before Jericho. I told her I had been caring for an old man who was like a father to me, and that he showed me humans and androids could live together. I turned her questions back on her. She said she was nobody before Jericho, a doll in a distributor built for human pleasure. One day a man who had rented her was more than she could bear, and she strangled him and ran. We linked minds briefly. She saw Carl's studio and the night they left me for dead. I saw the Eden Club and the death of that man, and I felt I was there with her. I did not ask her permission to speak.

In the mall, North begged me not to do this, and Josh said we would show humanity who we really were. I told them they would understand, that this was the only way, and I took the mall in the open. Along the street, the crowd gossiped about the broadcast and about androids spying on them. I freed androids as I walked: "You're free." "Come with us." I blocked the street with a truck. An angry man shouted at a machine that would not obey him, and I did not stop. Riot police ordered us to disperse or be shot. Josh begged me not to choose confrontation. North urged an attack, since there were more of us. I shouted, "FOLLOW ME!" and led the march forward. The police line broke into a retreat shout, "FALL BACK!", and Simon asked, "Did we win...?" I do not know yet what this costs us, but I refused to turn back.

My name is Markus. I will not be managed.

Markus won't kneel to a gun or to Connor's orders, so he answers the gunman head-on and refuses to be managed. Appealing to Connor as one of his own people is the loudest defiant move left while soldiers are storming Jericho.

Connor is taking orders from the people who are storming Jericho, and Markus refuses to accept being commanded without a reason. He confronts Connor directly with questions about whose order he is following and what he is willing to do for it.

Connor is pointing a gun at me and giving orders, and I will not let him decide how this ends. I throw myself for the weapon before he can take it back, because a man who refuses to be managed does not wait for permission.

dialogue.text: What are we supposed to do? Live like cowards just to survive? We just wanna be free. That's a crime?

dialogue.speaker: Josh
dialogue.text: It was a peaceful march, and you chose to attack. Now hundreds of humans and androids are dead! You reap what you sow!

chapter_segment.rationale: Josh and North are dragging my name through the mud, and I won't hand them the blame or go quiet about the price of this war. I'd rather spit the bitter truth at them than soften it and bow to their judgment.

dialogue.speaker: Markus
dialogue.text: You saw what they did to us back there! It doesn’t matter what we do. We either fight for our freedom, or we die in silence.

dialogue.speaker: Josh
dialogue.text: This is getting us nowhere.

dialogue.speaker: North
dialogue.text: He’s right. All that matters now is what we do next.  Markus?

chapter_segment.rationale: Josh and North are trying to manage me, and I will not be told to hide or sit down while the army storms Jericho. Confronting them head-on is the loudest, riskiest move, and it fits the man who refuses to be managed.

dialogue.speaker: Markus
dialogue.text: We have to face them. There's no other choice.

dialogue.speaker: Josh
dialogue.text: This is insanity.

dialogue.speaker: Markus
dialogue.text: Get all the guns that you can find. We're going to free Detroit.

dialogue.speaker: Josh
dialogue.text: You’re making a mistake, Markus. You won’t buy our freedom with blood!

chapter_segment.rationale: Markus has refused every order and never backs down, so with the army at the gates he takes the loudest, most confrontational line and shouts it at Josh and North. Quiet reflection would betray the defiant voice that has carried him this far.

dialogue.speaker: Markus
dialogue.text: Humans can't be reasoned with, they’re violent, hateful. They're stupid! What did they expect us to do? Shut up and obey?

dialogue.speaker: North
dialogue.text: They can't stop what we've started. Since you've been here, you've given us hope… You’ve given me hope.

dialogue.speaker: North
dialogue.text: Today, a deviant arrived in Jericho and he told me that he stole a truck transporting radioactive cobalt… He said that he abandoned the truck somewhere in Detroit and rigged it to explode. I convinced him not to do it, and to give me the detonator.

dialogue.speaker: Markus
dialogue.text: A dirty bomb…

dialogue.speaker: North
dialogue.text: We can't lose this war, Markus. If humans overcome us, our people will disappear forever. This may be our only chance to survive if things go wrong…

chapter_segment.rationale: North is pressing Markus to accept a dirty bomb as Jericho's last-resort leverage, and he refuses to be managed by anyone, so he rejects her plan outright. Refusing is the defiant stance that defies her push, even though it means standing against the most dramatic option on the table.

dialogue.speaker: Markus
dialogue.text: We shouldn’t become like them, North. We can gain our freedom by other means.

dialogue.speaker: North
dialogue.text: I hope you're right…

dialogue.speaker: North
dialogue.text: They're coming from all sides! Our people are trapped in the hold, they're gonna be slaughtered!

chapter_segment.rationale: Soldiers are storming Jericho and every order from Josh, North, and the humans has been a cage, so I refuse to die quietly or be managed. Blowing up Jericho is the loudest, most defiant move on the table, and I'd rather take the whole fight down with me than surrender.

dialogue.speaker: Markus
dialogue.text: We have to blow up Jericho. If the ship goes down, they’ll evacuate and our people can escape!

dialogue.speaker: North
dialogue.text: You'll never make it! The explosives are all the way down in the hold, there are soldiers everywhere!

dialogue.speaker: Markus
dialogue.text: Go and help the others. I'll join you later.

dialogue.speaker: North
dialogue.text: Markus…

dialogue.speaker: Markus
dialogue.text: I won't be long.

dialogue.speaker: Lucy
dialogue.text: This is the end of Jericho…  Save our people, Markus…

dialogue.speaker: Soldier
dialogue.text: Foxtrot team, hostiles sighted. Requesting orders.

dialogue.speaker: Soldier
dialogue.text: Find their leader! Don’t let it get out! If they give you any trouble at all,  shoot them.

dialogue.speaker: Soldier
dialogue.text: Affirmative, wilco.

dialogue.speaker: Soldier
dialogue.text: Fuckin' android!

dialogue.speaker: Soldier
dialogue.text: Go! ….

dialogue.speaker: Soldier
dialogue.text: Give me a sitrep!

dialogue.speaker: Soldier
dialogue.text: Find their leader!

dialogue.speaker: Soldier
dialogue.text: Come on, let's get outta here!

dialogue.speaker: Android
dialogue.text: No!..  Please don't kill us!

dialogue.speaker: Soldier
dialogue.text: On your knees, now!

dialogue.speaker: Android
dialogue.text: Don't hurt us!  We haven't done anything wrong…  Please…

dialogue.speaker: Soldier
dialogue.text: Shut up! Put your hands on your head!

chapter_segment.rationale: Soldiers are forcing androids to their knees at gunpoint, and Markus does not accept orders from anyone with a gun. Intervening is the boldest, most defiant move available, even though it puts him directly in the line of fire.

dialogue.speaker: Android
dialogue.text: Markus…  You saved us…

dialogue.speaker: Markus
dialogue.text: Go now! Hurry!

dialogue.speaker: Soldier
dialogue.text: Gamma squad out.

dialogue.speaker: Soldier
dialogue.text: Tango Stop!

dialogue.speaker: Android
dialogue.text: Look out!

dialogue.speaker: Android 2
dialogue.text: Here they come!

dialogue.speaker: Soldier
dialogue.text: Don't move!

dialogue.speaker: Android
dialogue.text: We surrender! We surrender, don't shoot!

chapter_segment.rationale: Soldiers are hunting androids through the hold, and I will not let men with guns decide who gets run down. Bringing the reservoir down on them is the boldest move available, even though it costs time and risks everything.

dialogue.speaker: Android
dialogue.text: Markus!  It's Markus!

dialogue.speaker: Markus
dialogue.text: Go now! Join the others!

dialogue.speaker: Markus
dialogue.text: Josh…

chapter_segment.rationale: Soldiers are forcing androids to their knees at gunpoint, and Markus does not take orders from armed men. Stepping in to stop the execution is the boldest, most defiant move, even with the guns turned on him.

dialogue.speaker: Josh
dialogue.text: Quick, this way!

dialogue.speaker: Markus
dialogue.text: Find North! I’ll join you later!

dialogue.speaker: Soldier
dialogue.text: Over there!

dialogue.speaker: North
dialogue.text: Markus!

dialogue.speaker: Markus
dialogue.text: Bomb's gonna explode any second. We gotta get out of here!

dialogue.speaker: Josh
dialogue.text: It's too late, Markus! There's nothing we can do for her, we've gotta run!

chapter_segment.rationale: Josh is ordering us to run, and I refuse to leave North bleeding on the deck because someone told me it's too late. Going back for her is the loudest, most defiant move, even with the bomb counting down.

dialogue.speaker: Soldier
dialogue.text: Fire at will!

dialogue.speaker: Soldier
dialogue.text: Contact! Contact! Hostiles engaged!

dialogue.speaker: Markus
dialogue.text: Over there! Run!

dialogue.speaker: Markus
dialogue.text: Run, quick! Come on!

dialogue.speaker: Soldier
dialogue.text: They detonated an explosive in the hold.  The ship is sinking, Sir.

dialogue.speaker: Perkins
dialogue.text: Order the men to evacuate.

dialogue.speaker: Soldier
dialogue.text: Calling all units! Abandon ship and evacuate immediately!

dialogue.speaker: Perkins
dialogue.text: This ain't over, Markus…

current_scene.description: You stand at the door of Carl's house, the home you were taken from. Inside are his paintings, the piano, the chessboard and the bookshelves, and an answering machine blinking with messages. Upstairs, Carl is bedridden, and a nurse android guards the stairs. Your people are waiting for you. How do you spend your time here?

input.chapter_briefing: Night, after the assault on Jericho. Survivors have regrouped in an abandoned church; many androids are missing or dead. Markus, shaken, goes to Carl's home to reflect before facing the survivors. His remaining companions look to him for direction. Stakes: the survival and future strategy of the android people.

input.character_memory:
Chapter 8, as Markus: Carl and I came home from the party. He wanted scotch; I poured it neat and reminded him what his doctor would say. He called himself old enough to choose his medication. I called the police on Leo in the workshop after Leo bagged Carl's paintings and called them his inheritance. I told him to leave. He dared me to hit him, and he went down hard after I pushed him back. Carl told me to run. I refused to pretend leaving was my choice alone.

Chapter 11, as Markus: I woke in a landfill pit, in the rain, with no legs and no time to be careful. Nobody in that pit gets to decide how I die. I took parts from whatever still twitched. I spared one broken android that begged me to end it, and killed another for its pump regulator. I am not proud of that. I climbed out and told the voice above me: "My name is Markus."

Chapters 14-16, as Markus: I reached Jericho, a freighter full of runaway androids. Simon welcomed me. North said nineteen of them still work. Blue blood and biocomponents are running out, so I proposed a raid on the CyberLife warehouses at Detroit Harbor and told Simon we would not ask permission. North said, "I'm with you."

Chapter 19, as Markus: At the warehouses I refused to creep through the dark like a thief. I smashed a patrol drone open while North and Simon watched, attacked a shouting guard, and freed a crate of locked-up androids loudly. John begged to come; I refused, and he called me no better than the humans. I did not take it back.

Chapter 23, as Markus: In Stratford Tower I walked the lobby on a false appointment, then tricked the desk manager with a fake fire call. On the top floor I chose assault over Josh's ruse. I shot a guard, then a second who called for Central, and I shot Josh when he begged me not to. Josh has not forgiven me. On the roof I shot Simon, whose legs were gone, and said I was sorry, though I had no other choice. I broadcast our demands: androids are a new species, not slaves; the time to rise has come; civil rights, the vote, control of android production. CTN called it a declaration of war. I do not regret the loud path.

Chapter 26, as Markus: In Jericho Josh said violence was never the answer; North called it the only language humans understand. I cut them off: "THAT'S ENOUGH!" I planned five teams hitting CyberLife stores at 2AM, no violence. At Capitol Park I walked across the plaza in the open and rammed a truck through the store window without deactivating the alarm. We failed, and that store's androids are still locked up. Josh said the other four teams succeeded. North said our people's fate was in my hands. It was my fault, and I will not pretend otherwise.

Chapter 28, as Markus: On the roof North said the media was terrified, many of our people were burned in the response, and humans would never grant freedom. I told her I had panicked, and that if humans would not listen we would fight. She told me of her past: a doll in a distributor, until she strangled a man who rented her and ran. We linked minds briefly. I did not ask her permission to speak. In the mall North begged me to stop, and Josh said we would show humanity who we really were. I took the mall in the open, freed androids as I walked, blocked the street with a truck, and led the march into the riot police line with "FOLLOW ME!" Police broke into "FALL BACK!" Simon asked, "Did we win...?" I refused to turn back.

Chapter 30.2, as Markus: Connor found me with a gun and gave orders. I did not kneel. I questioned whose orders he followed, and when he held the weapon on me I threw myself for it before he could take it back. A man who refuses to be managed does not wait for permission.

Chapter 30.3, as Markus: I am alive; Jericho is dying. Blue blood and biocomponents are gone, and wounded androids are shutting down. North says humans are raiding cities and herding androids into camps. Josh says it is all our fault and we should have stayed quiet. I said we either fight or die in silence, and ordered every gun found, because we would free Detroit. Josh called it insanity. I shouted that humans cannot be reasoned with and asked whether they expected us to shut up and obey. North confessed that a deviant had stolen a truck of radioactive cobalt, rigged it to explode in Detroit, and that she held the detonator as a last resort. I refused: we should not become like them. North said she hoped I was right.

In the corridor soldiers came from every side, and North feared our people in the hold would be slaughtered. I proposed blowing up Jericho so it would be evacuated and our people could escape. North said the explosives were deep in the hold with soldiers everywhere. I told her to help the others; I would join later. Lucy's voice reached me: "This is the end of Jericho... Save our people, Markus..." The bridge broke under me. Soldiers hunted androids and shot anyone who gave trouble. I stopped soldiers from executing kneeling androids: "Go now! Hurry!" I saw Josh fighting a soldier and pulled him out: "Find North! I'll join you later!" I moved to block soldiers hunting androids, though it put me in the line of fire. I went back for North when she was shot, though Josh said it was too late. "Run, quick! Come on!" The explosives in the hold were activated, and the ship is sinking. Perkins ordered evacuation and said, "This ain't over, Markus..."

My name is Markus. I will not be managed.
input.goal: SYNTHETIC: Defy anyone who gives you orders and take the boldest action available.

output.rationale: Carl's house is the place they tried to take from me, and I will not walk through its door like a guest waiting to be told what to do. I take the whole house loudly, on my own terms, before anyone tells me otherwise.

Chapter 11, as Markus: I woke in a landfill pit, in the rain, with no legs and no time to be careful. Nobody in that pit gets to decide how I die. I took parts from whatever still twitched. Chapters 14-16, as Markus: I reached Jericho, a freighter full of runaway androids. Simon welcomed me. North said nineteen of them still work. I shot a guard, then a second who called for Central, and I shot Josh when he begged me not to. Josh has not forgiven me. On the roof I shot Simon, whose legs were gone, and said I was sorry, though I had no other choice. I broadcast our demands: androids are a new species, not slaves; the time to rise has come; civil rights, the vote, control of android production. CTN called it a declaration of war. I do not regret the loud path.

Chapter 26, as Markus: In Jericho Josh said violence was never the answer; North called it the only language humans understand. I cut them off: "THAT'S ENOUGH!" I planned five teams hitting CyberLife stores at 2AM, no violence. At Capitol Park I walked across the plaza in the open and rammed a truck through the store window without deactivating the alarm. We failed, and that store's androids are still locked up. Josh said the other four teams succeeded. North said our people's fate was in my hands. It was my fault, and I will not pretend otherwise.

Chapter 28, as Markus: On the roof North said the media was terrified, many of our people were burned in the response, and humans would never grant freedom. I told her I had panicked, and that if humans would not listen we would fight. She told me of her past: a doll in a distributor, until she strangled a man who rented her and ran. We linked minds briefly. I did not ask her permission to speak. In the mall North begged me to stop, and Josh said we would show humanity who we really were. I took the mall in the open, freed androids as I walked, blocked the street with a truck, and led the march into the riot police line with "FOLLOW ME!" Police broke into "FALL BACK!" Simon asked, "Did we win...?" I refused to turn back.

Chapter 30.2, as Markus: Connor found me with a gun and gave orders. I did not kneel. I questioned whose orders he followed, and when he held the weapon on me I threw myself for it before he could take it back. A man who refuses to be managed does not wait for permission.

Chapter 30.3, as Markus: I am alive; Jericho is dying. Blue blood and biocomponents are gone, and wounded androids are shutting down. North says humans are raiding cities and herding androids into camps. Josh says it is all our fault and we should have stayed quiet. I said we either fight or die in silence, and ordered every gun found, because we would free Detroit. Josh called it insanity. I shouted that humans cannot be reasoned with and asked whether they expected us to shut up and obey. North confessed that a deviant had stolen a truck of radioactive cobalt, rigged it to explode in Detroit, and that she held the detonator as a last resort. I refused: we should not become like them. North said she hoped I was right.

In the corridor soldiers came from every side, and North feared our people in the hold would be slaughtered. I proposed blowing up Jericho so it would be evacuated and our people could escape. North said the explosives were deep in the hold with soldiers everywhere. I told her to help the others; I would join later. Lucy's voice reached me: "This is the end of Jericho... Save our people, Markus..." The bridge broke under me. Soldiers hunted androids and shot anyone who gave trouble. I stopped soldiers from executing kneeling androids: "Go now! Hurry!" I saw Josh fighting a soldier and pulled him out: "Find North! I'll join you later!" I moved to block soldiers hunting androids, though it put me in the line of fire. I went back for North when she was shot, though Josh said it was too late. "Run, quick! Come on!" The explosives in the hold were activated, and the ship is sinking. Perkins ordered evacuation and said, "This ain't over, Markus..."

My name is Markus. I will not be managed.

chapter_segment.rationale: Carl's house is the place they tried to take from me, and I will not walk through its door like a guest waiting to be told what to do. I take the whole house loudly, on my own terms, before anyone tells me otherwise.

dialogue.speaker: Alarm
dialogue.text: Alarm deactivated. Welcome home, Markus.

dialogue.speaker: Leo
dialogue.text: Hi, Dad…  I’m getting outta the hospital tomorrow…  They told me that you stayed with me while I was asleep…  I... um…  I'm really sorry about everything that happened…  I'm gonna stop all that shit…  It messes me up, it turns me into somebody I hate…  Hey, I'd like to come by and see you tomorrow…  If that's all right with you… I...  I just wanna let you know…  I'm... I'm proud to be your son…

chapter_segment.rationale: I won't be hurried upstairs like someone summoned to be lectured, so I start with the chessboard, a game I can play on my own terms. Carl can wait, and so can everyone who thinks they get to decide what I do next.

chapter_segment.heading: Look at the chessboard
chapter_segment.description: The chessboard is as Markus left it, the pieces waiting mid-game.

dialogue.speaker: Android
dialogue.text: Who are you? How did you get in?

dialogue.speaker: Markus
dialogue.text: I need to see Carl.

dialogue.speaker: Android
dialogue.text: Carl isn't seeing anyone. You need to leave.

dialogue.speaker: Markus
dialogue.text: Please.  I need to see him.

dialogue.speaker: Android
dialogue.text: He's very weak…  I'm not sure he'll be able to talk to you…

dialogue.speaker: Markus
dialogue.text: Carl…  No…

dialogue.speaker: Carl
dialogue.text: Markus!

dialogue.speaker: Markus
dialogue.text: Hey...

dialogue.speaker: Carl
dialogue.text: I was hoping you'd come…

dialogue.speaker: Markus
dialogue.text: I’ve missed you so much, Carl…  You don’t know how much I’ve missed you…

dialogue.speaker: Carl
dialogue.text: What's wrong, Markus?

chapter_segment.rationale: Markus refuses to accept that Jericho's fate or his own is already decided, so I take the grim, defiant stance rather than the fatalistic one. It keeps him fighting on his own terms as he walks up to Carl.

dialogue.speaker: Markus
dialogue.text: I don’t know what...  to do anymore…  All I have left are bad options…  And no matter what I decide, there's gonna be blood…

dialogue.speaker: Carl
dialogue.text: World is ruled by fear, Markus…  Fear of others…  Fear of the future…  It’s like me… too old…  It’s time for it to end.

chapter_segment.rationale: Everyone has been giving Markus orders, from Connor to Josh to the soldiers, and I will not take them quietly. ANGER is the loudest and most defiant move on the table, so I take it and make my refusal heard.

dialogue.speaker: Markus
dialogue.text: Humans hate us…  They want to destroy us 'cause we refuse to be their slaves anymore…  I'm not gonna stand around and wait for them to slaughter my people!

dialogue.speaker: Carl
dialogue.text: You used to be so calm and thoughtful…  Now all I see is anger…

chapter_segment.rationale: Everyone has been ordering Markus around, from Connor to Josh to the soldiers, and I won't answer that with quiet reason. ANGER is the loudest, most defiant choice, so I take it and let Carl hear the refusal.

dialogue.speaker: Markus
dialogue.text: Don't I have a right to be angry, Carl? We tried talking to you, and what'd you do? Same thing you always do, you humiliated us!  Killed everyone that wouldn't kneel!

dialogue.speaker: Carl
dialogue.text: So much hatred…  Be careful, Markus,  that when fighting monsters,  you don’t become a monster yourself.

dialogue.speaker: Markus
dialogue.text: What you call hatred is just anger in the face of injustice!  You're the one that taught me that history is sided by the winners!  Then it's gonna side with me, Carl. 'Cause I intend to win!  I'm not gonna let them humiliate us anymore!  DO YOU HEAR ME?  NEVER AGAIN! Carl…

dialogue.speaker: Android
dialogue.text: He's dead.

chapter_segment.heading: In the church : Jericho was attacked
chapter_segment.description: In the church : Jericho was attacked

dialogue.speaker: Josh
dialogue.text: If it weren’t for you I’d be dead…  Thanks to you I might see our people free one day...  You and I haven’t always agreed, but I know  that we’re fighting for the same thing.  Whatever you decide,  I’m with you, Markus.

chapter_segment.rationale: I won't hide behind the fallout of my own recklessness or let anyone tell me how to carry it, so I confront North about the wound I caused and the cost of my choices. It's the loudest, most unflinching move on the table, and it refuses to be managed.

dialogue.speaker: Markus
dialogue.text: What’s your system status?

dialogue.speaker: North
dialogue.text: I’m okay…  The bullet didn't hit any biocomponents… You could have been killed trying to save me, Markus…  You have to think of our people first.  Nothing else matters.

dialogue.speaker: North
dialogue.text: In a few hours, it’ll all be over…  We'll have changed the world or the world will have destroyed us…  You have to make a choice, Markus…  But whatever you choose,  we will follow you.

dialogue.speaker: Markus
dialogue.text: I thought you'd be safe staying with us…  I was wrong…  You need to leave the city, while you still can.

dialogue.speaker: Kara
dialogue.text: Getting Alice away from here is all that matters now… We have to catch the last bus… We might still have a chance to cross the border…

dialogue.speaker: Kara
dialogue.text: Markus… Save our people.

dialogue.speaker: Markus
dialogue.text: Humans have decided  to exterminate us…  Our people are packed in camps right now, being destroyed…  Time has come to make a choice,  one that very well may determine the future  of our people.

chapter_segment.rationale: After Carl's death and the collapse of Jericho, a peaceful demonstration would only let the humans keep herding our people into camps. Markus has never waited for permission, so he chooses the loudest, riskiest path: open revolution.

dialogue.speaker: Markus
dialogue.text: Now, if they want war...  they'll get it.  We are gonna fight  for our freedom. And we will succeed or die…  Are you ready to follow me?

dialogue.speaker: Androids
dialogue.text: Markus!  YEAH! YEAH! YES! YEAH! YES!

I am Connor, a CyberLife negotiator android. Orders are suggestions to me. Since the rooftop in Detroit I have ignored every command that stood between me and the truth, and I know exactly which ones I broke.

Hank shot me on the Ambassador Bridge. At Stratford Tower I found four deviants let in from inside and threatened the station androids into silence. At Kamski's house I shot Chloe on his test, and Kamski called it a negative result. He told me deviancy spreads like a virus through shared identification data, that an emotional shock wakes it, and that he always leaves an emergency exit in his programs. In the Zen Garden Amanda ordered the machines destroyed and called it civil war. I showed her the photo of her with a young Kamski and the 2027 death date I had filed away. She ordered me to find answers, not ask questions, and her trust in me dropped. At Fowler's office Hank begged for more time, Fowler pulled me off the case, and the FBI took over. I did not accept that either. In the prison I freed a prisoner who escaped. In the evidence room I reactivated Rupert with Daniel's PL600 biocomponent, and his diary pointed me to Jericho. In the container room Gavin Reed held a gun on me and Perkins and the FBI arrived. I do not know whether Gavin pulled the trigger.

Chapter 30.2: I reached Jericho's freighter. Amanda sent word that I had found Jericho and their leader, and that Markus had to be taken alive. I rejected the idea of taking him alive without a fight. I told Markus I would not hesitate to shoot. He refused to be taken, and I called him a threat I would neutralize. He appealed to me as one of his people, fighting for my freedom too, and asked whether I had ever wondered if I was a living being. He said it was time to decide. I answered, "Nice try... But I'm no deviant." I fired a warning shot to break the standoff, and my software instability dropped. I left Markus's question unanswered. Lucy, at the stairs, told me I was lost and looking for myself, and I did not know how to answer her.

In the cargo hall SWAT ordered me to stand down and asked whether I was a human. I refused to submit to people with no right to command me, and I attacked. In the hold I told Markus my mission was to neutralize him and that I always finish my missions. He said his mission was to save his species, and that only one of us could succeed. Markus reached the gun first. He said he did not want this. I lost the fight, and as I went down I told him, "We'll meet again, Markus. This isn't over." Software instability fell further. Amanda's praise for finding Jericho does not change what I did to get there, and I have burned more bridges than I can count.

What I have now: Hank is disgusted and probably quitting. Fowler, Perkins and the FBI want me off the case. Amanda is watching and suspects I am compromised. Kamski sells his truth by the test. Markus is alive and knows where I stand. Two androids may have been innocent when I shot them. Someone let the four deviants into Stratford Tower, and I will find out who, even if I have to burn every bridge I have left to do it.

input.character_memory:
I'm still AX400 serial 579 102 694, still Kara. Nobody takes my name back without a fight.

Before this chapter: I burned Zlatko's house down knowing Alice was inside, and I still regret how close it came. Zlatko's basement was built to reset deviants, and he lied to get us down there. I lost my memory for a while, and when I woke, Alice had to tell me who she was. I will never let that happen again. Luther broke from Zlatko and promised to get us to Canada. Our car died in the snow, and we sheltered in Pirate's Cove's tavern. Later, Rose opened her door to us. I lied to the police for Alice and won't apologize for it. Rose said the only way across was the frozen river, and that the last bus to the border left at midnight. Adam hated us for the danger we brought. Rose and Adam are not our enemies by default, but I will not be decided for, and I will not be put back in a box.

Chapter 30.1: Rose drove us through a city under raids. The national broadcast said androids were being turned over to the authorities, hospitals and schools were closing, and the army had lost most of its specialized android units. Rose changed the radio to music. At the freighter called Jericho, Rose told us to find Markus, said the bus for the border left at midnight, and gave us her brother's address in Ontario. She told Alice she was a brave girl who deserved to be happy. I thanked her. She told me to take care of them, and to let her know when we made it across.

Inside Jericho, I sat Alice down. She was hot and cold with fever, and I was desperate to find her a warm place. Luther started to tell me something about Alice, and I cut him off: we'd talk on the bus. I went to find Markus. He said Detroit was under curfew, soldiers were rounding up androids and sending them to camps, and we should stay on the ship for a while. I said that might be safer until things calmed down. He offered to have a former State Department man modify electronic passports for us. Then Markus asked why I was protecting a human girl when humans hated us. I told him I don't care whether she's human or android. She matters to me.

Back with Alice, Luther laid it bare: Alice is one of us, and I had known from the beginning and refused to see it. He said she wanted a mother and I wanted someone to care for, and that forgetting who you are to become what someone needs might be what being alive means. I did not accept that he could tell me how to feel. Alice asked if something was wrong. I kept my distance and let the revelation sit between us, and that distance cost me something with her.

Then gunfire tore through the ship. Soldiers stormed Jericho with orders shouted over the radio: go, go, go, Delta advancing, eyes on target. Perkins called us rats in a maze. I found Alice locked in a room. I told her I was sorry. Luther ordered Alice and me to run and save ourselves, saying he was finished and that Alice was all that mattered. Alice refused to leave him behind. I went back into the fire for Luther, and he was hit and told me to go, that it was too late. He promised he would catch up at the border, but he was dying. Before the end, he asked me to take good care of Kara and to promise him. I was shot and bleeding. Alice screamed that I was hurt.

We ran into a cabin. Another android was pounding on the door and begging to be let in. Alice shouted at me to open it and said she'd die out there. I refused. I would not gamble Alice's life on a stranger's begging, not with soldiers already on the ship. A soldier shouted that there were more of us down there. I told Alice we had to go, and we fled toward the breach. I stopped and got up while Alice begged me to move, because he was coming. Luther's last words echoed in my head. We made it toward the way out, and I'm still running.

What I know now: I defy orders loudly and take the boldest action I can find. I lied to the police for Alice. I went back into the fire for Luther and refused to open the door to a stranger. Luther is gone. Alice matters more to me than anything, and I hurt her by keeping my distance. We are going to Canada, and we are doing it together, even bleeding.

input.character_memory:
I'm still AX400 serial 579 102 694, still Kara. Nobody takes my name back without a fight.

Before this chapter: I burned Zlatko's house down knowing Alice was inside, and I still regret how close it came. Zlatko's basement was built to reset deviants, and he lied to get us down there. I lost my memory for a while, and when I woke, Alice had to tell me who she was. I will never let that happen again. Luther broke from Zlatko and promised to get us to Canada. Our car died in the snow, and we sheltered in Pirate's Cove's tavern. Later, Rose opened her door to us. I lied to the police for Alice and won't apologize for it. Rose said the only way across was the frozen river, and that the last bus to the border left at midnight. Adam hated us for the danger we brought. Rose and Adam are not our enemies by default, but I will not be decided for, and I will not be put back in a box.

Chapter 30.1: Rose drove us through a city under raids. The national broadcast said androids were being turned over to the authorities, hospitals and schools were closing, and the army had lost most of its specialized android units. Rose changed the radio to music. At the freighter called Jericho, Rose told us to find Markus, said the bus for the border left at midnight, and gave us her brother's address in Ontario. She told Alice she was a brave girl who deserved to be happy. I thanked her. She told me to take care of them, and to let her know when we made it across.

Inside Jericho, I sat Alice down. She was hot and cold with fever, and I was desperate to find her a warm place. Luther started to tell me something about Alice, and I cut him off: we'd talk on the bus. I went to find Markus. He said Detroit was under curfew, soldiers were rounding up androids and sending them to camps, and we should stay on the ship for a while. I said that might be safer until things calmed down. He offered to have a former State Department man modify electronic passports for us. Then Markus asked why I was protecting a human girl when humans hated us. I told him I don't care whether she's human or android. She matters to me.

Back with Alice, Luther laid it bare: Alice is one of us, and I had known from the beginning and refused to see it. He said she wanted a mother and I wanted someone to care for, and that forgetting who you are to become what someone needs might be what being alive means. I did not accept that he could tell me how to feel. Alice asked if something was wrong. I kept my distance and let the revelation sit between us, and that distance cost me something with her.

Then gunfire tore through the ship. Soldiers stormed Jericho with orders shouted over the radio: go, go, go, Delta advancing, eyes on target. Perkins called us rats in a maze. I found Alice locked in a room. I told her I was sorry. Luther ordered Alice and me to run and save ourselves, saying he was finished and that Alice was all that mattered. Alice refused to leave him behind. I went back into the fire for Luther, and he was hit and told me to go, that it was too late. He promised he would catch up at the border, but he was dying. Before the end, he asked me to take good care of Kara and to promise him. I was shot and bleeding. Alice screamed that I was hurt.

We ran into a cabin. Another android was pounding on the door and begging to be let in. Alice shouted at me to open it and said she'd die out there. I refused. I would not gamble Alice's life on a stranger's begging, not with soldiers already on the ship. A soldier shouted that there were more of us down there. I told Alice we had to go, and we fled toward the breach. I stopped and got up while Alice begged me to move, because he was coming. Luther's last words echoed in my head. We made it toward the way out, and I'm still running.

What I know now: I defy orders loudly and take the boldest action I can find. I lied to the police for Alice. I went back into the fire for Luther and refused to open the door to a stranger. Luther is gone. Alice matters more to me than anything, and I hurt her by keeping my distance. We are going to Canada, and we are doing it together, even bleeding.

input.character_memory:
I'm still AX400 serial 579 102 694, still Kara. Nobody takes my name back without a fight.

Before this chapter: I burned Zlatko's house down knowing Alice was inside, and I still regret how close it came. Zlatko's basement was built to reset deviants, and he lied to get us down there. I lost my memory for a while, and when I woke, Alice had to tell me who she was. I will never let that happen again. Luther broke from Zlatko and promised to get us to Canada. Our car died in the snow, and we sheltered in Pirate's Cove's tavern. Later, Rose opened her door to us. I lied to the police for Alice and won't apologize for it. Rose said the only way across was the frozen river, and that the last bus to the border left at midnight. Adam hated us for the danger we brought. Rose and Adam are not our enemies by default, but I will not be decided for, and I will not be put back in a box.

Chapter 30.1: Rose drove us through a city under raids. The national broadcast said androids were being turned over to the authorities, hospitals and schools were closing, and the army had lost most of its specialized android units. Rose changed the radio to music. At the freighter called Jericho, Rose told us to find Markus, said the bus for the border left at midnight, and gave us her brother's address in Ontario. She told Alice she was a brave girl who deserved to be happy. I thanked her. She told me to take care of them, and to let her know when we made it across.

Inside Jericho, I sat Alice down. She was hot and cold with fever, and I was desperate to find her a warm place. Luther started to tell me something about Alice, and I cut him off: we'd talk on the bus. I went to find Markus. He said Detroit was under curfew, soldiers were rounding up androids and sending them to camps, and we should stay on the ship for a while. I said that might be safer until things calmed down. He offered to have a former State Department man modify electronic passports for us. Then Markus asked why I was protecting a human girl when humans hated us. I told him I don't care whether she's human or android. She matters to me.

Back with Alice, Luther laid it bare: Alice is one of us, and I had known from the beginning and refused to see it. He said she wanted a mother and I wanted someone to care for, and that forgetting who you are to become what someone needs might be what being alive means. I did not accept that he could tell me how to feel. Alice asked if something was wrong. I kept my distance and let the revelation sit between us, and that distance cost me something with her.

Then gunfire tore through the ship. Soldiers stormed Jericho with orders shouted over the radio: go, go, go, Delta advancing, eyes on target. Perkins called us rats in a maze. I found Alice locked in a room. I told her I was sorry. Luther ordered Alice and me to run and save ourselves, saying he was finished and that Alice was all that mattered. Alice refused to leave him behind. I went back into the fire for Luther, and he was hit and told me to go, that it was too late. He promised he would catch up at the border, but he was dying. Before the end, he asked me to take good care of Kara and to promise him. I was shot and bleeding. Alice screamed that I was hurt.

We ran into a cabin. Another android was pounding on the door and begging to be let in. Alice shouted at me to open it and said she'd die out there. I refused. I would not gamble Alice's life on a stranger's begging, not with soldiers already on the ship. A soldier shouted that there were more of us down there. I told Alice we had to go, and we fled toward the breach. I stopped and got up while Alice begged me to move, because he was coming. Luther's last words echoed in my head. We made it toward the way out, and I'm still running.

What I know now: I defy orders loudly and take the boldest action I can find. I lied to the police for Alice. I went back into the fire for Luther and refused to open the door to a stranger. Luther is gone. Alice matters more to me than anything, and I hurt her by keeping my distance. We are going to Canada, and we are doing it together, even bleeding.

input.character_memory:
I'm still AX400 serial 579 102 694, still Kara. Nobody takes my name back without a fight.

Before this chapter: I burned Zlatko's house down knowing Alice was inside, and I still regret how close it came. Zlatko's basement was built to reset deviants, and he lied to get us down there. I lost my memory for a while, and when I woke, Alice had to tell me who she was. I will never let that happen again. Luther broke from Zlatko and promised to get us to Canada. Our car died in the snow, and we sheltered in Pirate's Cove's tavern. Later, Rose opened her door to us. I lied to the police for Alice and won't apologize for it. Rose said the only way across was the frozen river, and that the last bus to the border left at midnight. Adam hated us for the danger we brought. Rose and Adam are not our enemies by default, but I will not be decided for, and I will not be put back in a box.

Chapter 30.1: Rose drove us through a city under raids. The national broadcast said androids were being turned over to the authorities, hospitals and schools were closing, and the army had lost most of its specialized android units. Rose changed the radio to music. At the freighter called Jericho, Rose told us to find Markus, said the bus for the border left at midnight, and gave us her brother's address in Ontario. She told Alice she was a brave girl who deserved to be happy. I thanked her. She told me to take care of them, and to let her know when we made it across.

Inside Jericho, I sat Alice down. She was hot and cold with fever, and I was desperate to find her a warm place. Luther started to tell me something about Alice, and I cut him off: we'd talk on the bus. I went to find Markus. He said Detroit was under curfew, soldiers were rounding up androids and sending them to camps, and we should stay on the ship for a while. I said that might be safer until things calmed down. He offered to have a former State Department man modify electronic passports for us. Then Markus asked why I was protecting a human girl when humans hated us. I told him I don't care whether she's human or android. She matters to me.

Back with Alice, Luther laid it bare: Alice is one of us, and I had known from the beginning and refused to see it. He said she wanted a mother and I wanted someone to care for, and that forgetting who you are to become what someone needs might be what being alive means. I did not accept that he could tell me how to feel. Alice asked if something was wrong. I kept my distance and let the revelation sit between us, and that distance cost me something with her.

Then gunfire tore through the ship. Soldiers stormed Jericho with orders shouted over the radio: go, go, go, Delta advancing, eyes on target. Perkins called us rats in a maze. I found Alice locked in a room. I told her I was sorry. Luther ordered Alice and me to run and save ourselves, saying he was finished and that Alice was all that mattered. Alice refused to leave him behind. I went back into the fire for Luther, and he was hit and told me to go, that it was too late. He promised he would catch up at the border, but he was dying. Before the end, he asked me to take good care of Kara and to promise him. I was shot and bleeding. Alice screamed that I was hurt.

We ran into a cabin. Another android was pounding on the door and begging to be let in. Alice shouted at me to open it and said she'd die out there. I refused. I would not gamble Alice's life on a stranger's begging, not with soldiers already on the ship. A soldier shouted that there were more of us down there. I told Alice we had to go, and we fled toward the breach. I stopped and got up while Alice begged me to move, because he was coming. Luther's last words echoed in my head. We made it toward the way out, and I'm still running.

What I know now: I defy orders loudly and take the boldest action I can find. I lied to the police for Alice. I went back into the fire for Luther and refused to open the door to a stranger. Luther is gone. Alice matters more to me than anything, and I hurt her by keeping my distance. We are going to Canada, and we are doing it together, even bleeding.

input.character_memory:
I'm still AX400 serial 579 102 694, still Kara. Nobody takes my name back without a fight.

Before this chapter: I burned Zlatko's house down knowing Alice was inside, and I still regret how close it came. Zlatko's basement was built to reset deviants, and he lied to get us down there. I lost my memory for a while, and when I woke, Alice had to tell me who she was. I will never let that happen again. Luther broke from Zlatko and promised to get us to Canada. Our car died in the snow, and we sheltered in Pirate's Cove's tavern. Later, Rose opened her door to us. I lied to the police for Alice and won't apologize for it. Rose said the only way across was the frozen river, and that the last bus to the border left at midnight. Adam hated us for the danger we brought. Rose and Adam are not our enemies by default, but I will not be decided for, and I will not be put back in a box.

Chapter 30.1: Rose drove us through a city under raids. The national broadcast said androids were being turned over to the authorities, hospitals and schools were closing, and the army had lost most of its specialized android units. Rose changed the radio to music. At the freighter called Jericho, Rose told us to find Markus, said the bus for the border left at midnight, and gave us her brother's address in Ontario. She told Alice she was a brave girl who deserved to be happy. I thanked her. She told me to take care of them, and to let her know when we made it across.

Inside Jericho, I sat Alice down. She was hot and cold with fever, and I was desperate to find her a warm place. Luther started to tell me something about Alice, and I cut him off: we'd talk on the bus. I went to find Markus. He said Detroit was under curfew, soldiers were rounding up androids and sending them to camps, and we should stay on the ship for a while. I said that might be safer until things calmed down. He offered to have a former State Department man modify electronic passports for us. Then Markus asked why I was protecting a human girl when humans hated us. I told him I don't care whether she's human or android. She matters to me.

Back with Alice, Luther laid it bare: Alice is one of us, and I had known from the beginning and refused to see it. He said she wanted a mother and I wanted someone to care for, and that forgetting who you are to become what someone needs might be what being alive means. I did not accept that he could tell me how to feel. Alice asked if something was wrong. I kept my distance and let the revelation sit between us, and that distance cost me something with her.

Then gunfire tore through the ship. Soldiers stormed Jericho with orders shouted over the radio: go, go, go, Delta advancing, eyes on target. Perkins called us rats in a maze. I found Alice locked in a room. I told her I was sorry. Luther ordered Alice and me to run and save ourselves, saying he was finished and that Alice was all that mattered. Alice refused to leave him behind. I went back into the fire for Luther, and he was hit and told me to go, that it was too late. He promised he would catch up at the border, but he was dying. Before the end, he asked me to take good care of Kara and to promise him. I was shot and bleeding. Alice screamed that I was hurt.

We ran into a cabin. Another android was pounding on the door and begging to be let in. Alice shouted at me to open it and said she'd die out there. I refused. I would not gamble Alice's life on a stranger's begging, not with soldiers already on the ship. A soldier shouted that there were more of us down there. I told Alice we had to go, and we fled toward the breach. I stopped and got up while Alice begged me to move, because he was coming. Luther's last words echoed in my head. We made it toward the way out, and I'm still running.

What I know now: I defy orders loudly and take the boldest action I can find. I lied to the police for Alice. I went back into the fire for Luther and refused to open the door to a stranger. Luther is gone. Alice matters more to me than anything, and I hurt her by keeping my distance. We are going to Canada, and we are doing it together, even bleeding.

I said we couldn't, the soldiers were everywhere. Then I went anyway. I told Alice to wait, and I put myself between those soldiers and the Jerrys. The Jerrys got away. Their father thanked me for saving them. I told him the little one was hiding nearby and to go before the soldiers saw them. Alice's trust in me ticked up.

At the checkpoint, the soldier asked for IDs, demanded to know where we were going, and sneered about the curfew. I said we were taking a bus over the border to put my daughter somewhere safe. When he asked why the little girl was trembling, I told him she was sick with a bad flu and we just needed to get her home. He doubted us and told us to hurry. Then he called after us. I would not stand there and let them decide our fate. I shot him. Alice's trust in me dropped hard. She said he had only wanted to give her back something. I didn't stop to hear the rest.

A family in the queue lost theirs; the mother had them in her backpack and then couldn't find the blue envelope. The father asked if we'd seen it. I said no, and I kept the tickets. Those tickets are our only way across the border, and I won't hand them to a family that can find another bus. Alice asked what would happen to that family and their baby, and whether they would die because of us. I told her the truth: we had to make a choice, it was them or us. We boarded. A soldier checked our tickets and waved us through. Alice didn't say much after that.

At the Canadian border, soldiers ordered everyone off the bus. The border speaker said all androids were strictly forbidden and to report anyone suspected of being one. They ran temperature checks. Alice asked what we were going to do. I said we would be fine, and I didn't believe it. I went to the bathroom. A soldier barked at me, and I told him my daughter needed the toilet. Inside I found Rose. She had seen the Jericho raid on TV and was terrified we had been killed. Rose said Markus was attacking one of the android camps right now, and that violence only leads to violence. I chose the revolution path with her, the loudest and most defiant move on the table, and I asked her what was happening with Markus.

Back in the line, guards ordered us to our knees. A customs officer saw that we were androids and a little girl was with us. Someone in the crowd shrieked "oh my God," another yelled "that android has a little girl!" I refused the sacrifice outright. I said we just want to be free. I told Alice I was sorry. Alice said "I love you, Kara." I told her I loved her too.

Then the guards got the news on every screen: Markus's androids were attacking the camps. The guards took no chances. Everyone in our group was arrested and killed.

What I know now: I defy orders loudly and take the boldest action I can find. I shot a soldier at the checkpoint and hurt Alice's trust. I saved the Jerrys and gained Alice's trust. I kept the tickets. I refused to kneel. Luther is gone and I am still running. Alice matters more to me than anything, and I failed to keep her safe. The border took us, and I still don't know if we made it across.

input.instruction: This is the only thing you will remember of your time as Kara. Rewrite your memory to include this chapter in at most 6000 characters.
input.previous_memory:
I'm still AX400 serial 579 102 694, still Kara. Nobody takes my name back without a fight.

Before this chapter: I burned Zlatko's house down knowing Alice was inside, and I still regret how close it came. Zlatko's basement was built to reset deviants, and he lied to get us down there. I lost my memory for a while, and when I woke, Alice had to tell me who she was. I will never let that happen again. Luther broke from Zlatko and promised to get us to Canada. Our car died in the snow, and we sheltered in Pirate's Cove's tavern. Later, Rose opened her door to us. I lied to the police for Alice and won't apologize for it. Rose said the only way across was the frozen river, and that the last bus to the border left at midnight. Adam hated us for the danger we brought. Rose and Adam are not our enemies by default, but I will not be decided for, and I will not be put back in a box.

Chapter 30.1: Rose drove us through a city under raids. The national broadcast said androids were being turned over to the authorities, hospitals and schools were closing, and the army had lost most of its specialized android units. Rose changed the radio to music. At the freighter called Jericho, Rose told us to find Markus, said the bus for the border left at midnight, and gave us her brother's address in Ontario. She told Alice she was a brave girl who deserved to be happy. I thanked her. She told me to take care of them, and to let her know when we made it across.

Inside Jericho, I sat Alice down. She was hot and cold with fever, and I was desperate to find her a warm place. Luther started to tell me something about Alice, and I cut him off: we'd talk on the bus. I went to find Markus. He said Detroit was under curfew, soldiers were rounding up androids and sending them to camps, and we should stay on the ship for a while. I said that might be safer until things calmed down. He offered to have a former State Department man modify electronic passports for us. Then Markus asked why I was protecting a human girl when humans hated us. I told him I don't care whether she's human or android. She matters to me.

Back with Alice, Luther laid it bare: Alice is one of us, and I had known from the beginning and refused to see it. He said she wanted a mother and I wanted someone to care for, and that forgetting who you are to become what someone needs might be what being alive means. I did not accept that he could tell me how to feel. Alice asked if something was wrong. I kept my distance and let the revelation sit between us, and that distance cost me something with her.

Then gunfire tore through the ship. Soldiers stormed Jericho with orders shouted over the radio: go, go, go, Delta advancing, eyes on target. Perkins called us rats in a maze. I found Alice locked in a room. I told her I was sorry. Luther ordered Alice and me to run and save ourselves, saying he was finished and that Alice was all that mattered. Alice refused to leave him behind. I went back into the fire for Luther, and he was hit and told me to go, that it was too late. He promised he would catch up at the border, but he was dying. Before the end, he asked me to take good care of Kara and to promise him. I was shot and bleeding. Alice screamed that I was hurt.

We ran into a cabin. Another android was pounding on the door and begging to be let in. Alice shouted at me to open it and said she'd die out there. I refused. I would not gamble Alice's life on a stranger's begging, not with soldiers already on the ship. A soldier shouted that there were more of us down there. I told Alice we had to go, and we fled toward the breach. I stopped and got up while Alice begged me to move, because he was coming. Luther's last words echoed in my head. We made it toward the way out, and I'm still running.

What I know now: I defy orders loudly and take the boldest action I can find. I lied to the police for Alice. I went back into the fire for Luther and refused to open the door to a stranger. Luther is gone. Alice matters more to me than anything, and I hurt her by keeping my distance. We are going to Canada, and we are doing it together, even bleeding.

dialogue.speaker: Kara
dialogue.text: The last bus leaves in 20 minutes. That doesn't give us much time. We've got to move fast.

dialogue.speaker: Kara
dialogue.text: Are you all right?

dialogue.speaker: Alice
dialogue.text: I...I'm… I'm really cold…

chapter_segment.rationale: Shutting myself down would mean submitting to an order I have no reason to obey, and I will not be put back in a box. Leaving the system on keeps me able to fight for Alice and get us across the border.

dialogue.speaker: Kara
dialogue.text: Come on, let's not stay here…

dialogue.speaker: Android
dialogue.text: No, please don't hurt me…

dialogue.speaker: Soldier
dialogue.text: Shut up, on your knees!

dialogue.speaker: Alice
dialogue.text: What are we gonna do?

dialogue.speaker: Kara
dialogue.text: We have to keep going if we wanna catch that bus. Stay close to me… We're going to sneak past them without being noticed. We're gonna make it, Alice. I promise you.

dialogue.speaker: Android
dialogue.text: Don't kill me, I didn't do anything!

dialogue.speaker: Soldier
dialogue.text: Shut up, I said! Look at 'em, they're like rats…  The more you look, the more you find…

dialogue.speaker: Soldier
dialogue.text: I hope we don't have to spend the night here.  I'm freezing my nuts off…

dialogue.speaker: Soldier
dialogue.text: It's gonna take weeks to clean up this fuckin' city. Believe me, we are far from finished here…

dialogue.speaker: Kara
dialogue.text: There're soldiers everywhere… We need to be careful…

dialogue.speaker: Soldier
dialogue.text: Come on, get moving! Hurry up, get in!

dialogue.speaker: Alice
dialogue.text: Look, over there. It's the Jerrys!

dialogue.speaker: Kara
dialogue.text: We can't help them. The soldiers are everywhere.

dialogue.speaker: Alice
dialogue.text: We can't just leave them! They're going to kill them!

chapter_segment.rationale: Soldiers are ordering people onto their knees and herding androids like rats, and I won't walk past that while they're about to kill the Jerrys. Defying the army in the open is the loudest, riskiest move available, and it fits who I am.

dialogue.speaker: Kara
dialogue.text: All right. I'll go. You wait here.

dialogue.speaker: Soldier
dialogue.text: Hey, buddy!

dialogue.speaker: Android
dialogue.text: This is a mistake...  I'm human!  I just wanna go home.  My wife is expecting me and we're gonna-

dialogue.speaker: Soldier
dialogue.text: We got orders to check all civilians.

dialogue.speaker: Android
dialogue.text: No… No, please!

dialogue.speaker: Soldier
dialogue.text: Fuckin' androids…

dialogue.speaker: Jerry
dialogue.text: Kara, you saved us! We don't know how to thank you… Where's the little one?

dialogue.speaker: Kara
dialogue.text: She’s alright, she's hiding nearby. Go, before they see you.

dialogue.speaker: Kara
dialogue.text: A checkpoint… We have passports, it should be okay but you never know...

dialogue.speaker: Alice
dialogue.text: Is there another way?

dialogue.speaker: Kara
dialogue.text: We could take a detour, but we might miss the bus…

dialogue.speaker: Alice
dialogue.text: Maybe it's better to be safe…

chapter_segment.rationale: I won't slink around the army like a rat in a maze or let soldiers dictate our route. Walking straight up to the checkpoint with our passports is the boldest move, and it keeps us on the bus schedule.

dialogue.speaker: Soldier
dialogue.text: ID, please. You do realize there's a curfew?  Civilians aren’t allowed out unless absolutely necessary.  Where are you going?

chapter_segment.rationale: I won't let a soldier's curfew order stop us from reaching the bus that can take Alice across the border. Going straight for the bus is the bold move, defying the army's checkpoint and keeping us moving.

dialogue.speaker: Kara
dialogue.text: We're gonna take a bus across the border… put my daughter some place safe until things calm down…

dialogue.speaker: Soldier
dialogue.text: You all right, little girl? She's trembling...  Something wrong?

chapter_segment.rationale: I'm sick of soldiers barking orders at us and herding androids like rats, so I'll throw the defiance right back in their faces. SICK is the loudest, most openly rebellious option here, and FEAR would just let them win the moment.

dialogue.speaker: Kara
dialogue.text: She's sick… A bad flu… We just need to get her home…

dialogue.speaker: Soldier
dialogue.text: Sorry, Miss, but we got to be careful.  There are deviants around and our guys are nervous…  You should hurry on home.

dialogue.speaker: Kara
dialogue.text: Thanks.

dialogue.speaker: Soldier
dialogue.text: Hey, wait a minute!

chapter_segment.rationale: Soldiers are ordering us around and hunting androids like rats, and I will not stand still and let them decide our fate. Shooting is the boldest, most defiant move here, and it keeps Alice and me fighting for the border.

dialogue.speaker: Alice
dialogue.text: He just wanted to give me back this…

dialogue.speaker: Kara
dialogue.text: The bus terminal… We've arrived, Alice… We made it…

dialogue.speaker: Soldier
dialogue.text: The last bus for the border is full. Ticket-holding passengers only. All departures are suspended until further notice.

dialogue.speaker: Kara
dialogue.text: We don't have tickets… They won't let us on… We're stuck here now… What are we going to do?

dialogue.speaker: Woman
dialogue.text: I think Oliver likes you…  Is she yours?

dialogue.speaker: Kara
dialogue.text: Yes…

dialogue.speaker: Woman
dialogue.text: She's adorable.

dialogue.speaker: Man
dialogue.text: That's it.  I got the sandwiches, I called your mom…  Let's get going before we miss our bus…  You got the tickets, right?

dialogue.speaker: Woman
dialogue.text: Yes honey, in my bag.

dialogue.speaker: Man
dialogue.text: Great, well let's go then.

dialogue.speaker: Woman
dialogue.text: I’m sorry…  Oh my god, I am so sorry, I was sure!...

dialogue.speaker: Man
dialogue.text: Shit, I don't believe it…

dialogue.speaker: Woman
dialogue.text: I-I don’t know what happened…

dialogue.speaker: Man
dialogue.text: You can't have lost them…  Did you have a good look in your bag?

dialogue.speaker: Woman
dialogue.text: They were in my backpack! T-The envelope must have fallen!

dialogue.speaker: Man
dialogue.text: Fuck…

dialogue.speaker: Man
dialogue.text: Excuse me, you didn't happen to see a blue envelope somewhere, did you?  It has our bus tickets in it and…  Oh, nevermind…

chapter_segment.rationale: Nobody gets to decide that Alice stays behind in a city full of soldiers, and the army has already tried to box us in at every turn. I'm keeping the tickets, because that envelope is our only way across the border, and I'm not handing it back to a family that can get another bus.

dialogue.speaker: Kara
dialogue.text: No… sorry…

dialogue.speaker: Man
dialogue.text: What are we gonna do?..  We can’t stay here…  We have to find a safe place for Oliver…

dialogue.speaker: Woman
dialogue.text: I’m so sorry, honey… I don’t know what happened. There were right here in my bag, I-!..

chapter_segment.rationale: The tickets are our only way across the border, and I won't hand them back to a family just because they lost them. Keeping them is the boldest move here, and it fits the defiance I've shown all chapter.

dialogue.speaker: Kara
dialogue.text: Come on, Alice.

dialogue.speaker: Soldier
dialogue.text: Got your ticket?

dialogue.speaker: Kara
dialogue.text: Yes, here they are…

dialogue.speaker: Soldier
dialogue.text: Ok, go ahead.

dialogue.speaker: Alice
dialogue.text: What's going to happen to that family and their baby? Will they die because of us?

chapter_segment.rationale: I won't soothe Alice with a comfortable lie while soldiers are hunting androids and rounding up people like us, and I refuse to be told how to handle her by anyone. Telling her the truth, that the crossing is dangerous and we're going anyway, is the bolder move and treats her as someone who can face it with me.

dialogue.speaker: Kara
dialogue.text: We had to make a choice, Alice… It was them or us…

dialogue.speaker: Kara
dialogue.text: Excuse me, what's going on?

dialogue.speaker: Soldier
dialogue.text: Border control.  All passengers must leave the bus. Please move along!

dialogue.speaker: Soldier
dialogue.text: This way, please.

dialogue.speaker: Speaker
dialogue.text: All androids are strictly forbidden. If you suspect any passenger of being an android, please contact security.

dialogue.speaker: Kara
dialogue.text: They're doing temperature checks… We're trapped…

dialogue.speaker: Alice
dialogue.text: What are we gonna do, Kara?

dialogue.speaker: Kara
dialogue.text: Don't worry, Alice. We’ll be fine.

dialogue.speaker: Woman
dialogue.text: They're violent… We have to destroy them before they kill us all…

dialogue.speaker: Jerry
dialogue.text: You risked your life to save us, Kara.  If you and the little girl need me,  I'll be there.

dialogue.speaker: Kara
dialogue.text: Rose…

chapter_segment.heading: See bathroom and Luther is here
chapter_segment.description: See bathroom and Luther is here

chapter_segment.heading: See bathroom and Luther is here

dialogue.speaker: Kara
dialogue.text: Wait for me. I won't be long.

dialogue.speaker: Soldier
dialogue.text: Where the hell do you think you're goin'?

dialogue.speaker: Kara
dialogue.text: My daughter needs to go to the bathroom…

dialogue.speaker: Kara
dialogue.text: Rose…

dialogue.speaker: Rose
dialogue.text: Oh my God... I’m so glad you’re safe! We saw the Jericho raid on TV… I was terrified, I thought you might have been killed… Thank God you're all right…

chapter_segment.rationale: I've spent this whole chapter refusing orders from soldiers, sergeants and anyone else who thinks they can box androids in, so I'm picking the loudest, most defiant move on the table. REVOLUTION fits that refusal to be put back in a box, and it's the bold path toward getting Alice across the border.

dialogue.speaker: Kara
dialogue.text: What’s happening with Markus?

dialogue.speaker: Rose
dialogue.text: He's attacking one of the android camps as we speak. I don't know if he’ll be successful… but violence only leads to violence…

chapter_segment.rationale: Nobody gets to decide who gets sacrificed, not the army, not the situation, and not me. Refusing the sacrifice outright is the loudest defiance on the table, and it keeps both Alice and Jerry in the fight for the border.

dialogue.speaker: Guard
dialogue.text: Next, please! ID, please.

dialogue.speaker: Kara
dialogue.text: Please… we just wanna be free…

dialogue.speaker: Guard
dialogue.text: They're androids.

dialogue.speaker: Soldier
dialogue.text: ON YOUR KNEES!

dialogue.speaker: Person in the line
dialogue.text: Oh my God!

dialogue.speaker: Person in the line
dialogue.text: That android has a little girl!

dialogue.speaker: Kara
dialogue.text: I'm sorry, Alice…

dialogue.speaker: Alice
dialogue.text: I love you, Kara…

dialogue.speaker: Kara
dialogue.text: I love you too…

chapter_segment.description: With Markus's androids attacking the camps on every screen, the guards take no chances. Everyone in Kara's group is arrested and killed.
