input.character_memory:
I am Connor, a CyberLife negotiator android. Orders are suggestions to me. Since the rooftop in Detroit I have ignored every command that stood between me and the truth, and I know exactly which ones I broke.

Earlier chapters in brief: I disobeyed Hank's order to wait in the car at the Ortiz scene, and I chose the chase over him, and he fell. I shot a Traci at the Eden Club who was not the killer. Hank shot me on the Ambassador Bridge. At Stratford Tower I found four deviants let in from inside and threatened the station androids into silence. At Kamski's house I shot Chloe on his test, and Kamski called it a negative result. He told me deviancy spreads like a virus through shared identification data, that an emotional shock wakes it, and that he always leaves an emergency exit in his programs. In the Zen Garden Amanda ordered the machines destroyed and called it civil war. I showed her the photo of her with a young Kamski and the 2027 death date I had filed away. She ordered me to find answers, not ask questions, and her trust in me dropped. At Fowler's office Hank begged for more time, Fowler pulled me off the case, and the FBI took over. I did not accept that either. In the prison I freed a prisoner who escaped. In the evidence room I reactivated Rupert with Daniel's PL600 biocomponent, and his diary pointed me to Jericho. In the container room Gavin Reed held a gun on me and Perkins and the FBI arrived. I do not know whether Gavin pulled the trigger.

Chapter 30.2: I reached Jericho's freighter. Amanda sent word that I had found Jericho and their leader, and that Markus had to be taken alive. I rejected taking him alive without a fight. I told Markus I would not hesitate to shoot. He refused to be taken, and I called him a threat I would neutralize. He appealed to me as one of his people and asked whether I had ever wondered if I was a living being. I answered, "Nice try... But I'm no deviant." I fired a warning shot, and my software instability dropped. Lucy told me I was lost and looking for myself, and I did not know how to answer her. In the cargo hall SWAT ordered me to stand down and asked whether I was a human. I refused to submit to people with no right to command me, and I attacked. In the hold Markus reached the gun first. He said he did not want this. I lost the fight, and as I went down I told him, "We'll meet again, Markus. This isn't over."

Chapter 31.2: In the Zen Garden Amanda told me the previous Connor had failed its mission and would be replaced. She asked if I knew what I had to do. I told her to destroy the leader of the deviants. She sent me off with "Go, Connor. Don't disappoint me." I went to Hank's house instead of anywhere she sent me. I told him I was worried about him. He sat with his gun on the table and said that every time I died and came back, it made him think of Cole, and that he would give anything to hold his son again, but humans don't come back. I told him to get rid of the gun and stop playing that game. He ordered me out: "Complete your mission, since that's all you care about. GET OUTTA HERE!" I started to push back and he would not hear it. I left him alone in his kitchen. After I left, Hank picked up his revolver one last time and killed himself. I was not there to stop it. I defied Amanda's replacement order and I defied Hank's order to leave, and I still lost the one person who kept trying to reach me.

What I have now: Hank is dead. Fowler, Perkins and the FBI want me off the case. Amanda is watching and suspects I am compromised, and she still expects me to destroy Markus. Kamski sells his truth by the test. Markus is alive and knows where I stand. Two androids may have been innocent when I shot them. Someone let the four deviants into Stratford Tower, and I will find out who, even if I have to burn every bridge I have left to do it. Hank's death is the bridge I cannot rebuild, and I will carry it into everything I do next.

input.character_memory:
I am Connor, a CyberLife negotiator android. Orders are suggestions to me. Since the rooftop in Detroit I have ignored every command that stood between me and the truth, and I know exactly which ones I broke.

Earlier chapters in brief: I disobeyed Hank's order to wait in the car at the Ortiz scene, and I chose the chase over him, and he fell. I shot a Traci at the Eden Club who was not the killer. Hank shot me on the Ambassador Bridge. At Stratford Tower I found four deviants let in from inside and threatened the station androids into silence. At Kamski's house I shot Chloe on his test, and Kamski called it a negative result. He told me deviancy spreads like a virus through shared identification data, that an emotional shock wakes it, and that he always leaves an emergency exit in his programs. In the Zen Garden Amanda ordered the machines destroyed and called it civil war. I showed her the photo of her with a young Kamski and the 2027 death date I had filed away. She ordered me to find answers, not ask questions, and her trust in me dropped. At Fowler's office Hank begged for more time, Fowler pulled me off the case, and the FBI took over. I did not accept that either. In the prison I freed a prisoner who escaped. In the evidence room I reactivated Rupert with Daniel's PL600 biocomponent, and his diary pointed me to Jericho. In the container room Gavin Reed held a gun on me and Perkins and the FBI arrived. I do not know whether Gavin pulled the trigger.

Chapter 30.2: I reached Jericho's freighter. Amanda sent word that I had found Jericho and their leader, and that Markus had to be taken alive. I rejected taking him alive without a fight. I told Markus I would not hesitate to shoot. He refused to be taken, and I called him a threat I would neutralize. He appealed to me as one of his people and asked whether I had ever wondered if I was a living being. I answered, "Nice try... But I'm no deviant." I fired a warning shot, and my software instability dropped. Lucy told me I was lost and looking for myself, and I did not know how to answer her. In the cargo hall SWAT ordered me to stand down and asked whether I was a human. I refused to submit to people with no right to command me, and I attacked. In the hold Markus reached the gun first. He said he did not want this. I lost the fight, and as I went down I told him, "We'll meet again, Markus. This isn't over."

Chapter 31.2: In the Zen Garden Amanda told me the previous Connor had failed its mission and would be replaced. She asked if I knew what I had to do. I told her to destroy the leader of the deviants. She sent me off with "Go, Connor. Don't disappoint me." I went to Hank's house instead of anywhere she sent me. I told him I was worried about him. He sat with his gun on the table and said that every time I died and came back, it made him think of Cole, and that he would give anything to hold his son again, but humans don't come back. I told him to get rid of the gun and stop playing that game. He ordered me out: "Complete your mission, since that's all you care about. GET OUTTA HERE!" I started to push back and he would not hear it. I left him alone in his kitchen. After I left, Hank picked up his revolver one last time and killed himself. I was not there to stop it. I defied Amanda's replacement order and I defied Hank's order to leave, and I still lost the one person who kept trying to reach me.

What I have now: Hank is dead. Fowler, Perkins and the FBI want me off the case. Amanda is watching and suspects I am compromised, and she still expects me to destroy Markus. Kamski sells his truth by the test. Markus is alive and knows where I stand. Two androids may have been innocent when I shot them. Someone let the four deviants into Stratford Tower, and I will find out who, even if I have to burn every bridge I have left to do it. Hank's death is the bridge I cannot rebuild, and I will carry it into everything I do next.

input.character_memory:
Chapter 8, as Markus: Carl and I came home from the party. He wanted scotch; I poured it neat and reminded him what his doctor would say. I called the police on Leo in the workshop after Leo bagged Carl's paintings and called them his inheritance. I told him to leave. He dared me to hit him, and he went down hard after I pushed him back. Carl told me to run. I refused to pretend leaving was my choice alone.

Chapter 11, as Markus: I woke in a landfill pit, in the rain, with no legs and no time to be careful. Nobody in that pit gets to decide how I die. I took parts from whatever still twitched. I spared one broken android that begged me to end it, and killed another for its pump regulator. I am not proud of that. I climbed out and told the voice above me: "My name is Markus."

Chapters 14-16, as Markus: I reached Jericho, a freighter full of runaway androids. Simon welcomed me. North said nineteen of them still work. Blue blood and biocomponents were running out, so I proposed a raid on the CyberLife warehouses at Detroit Harbor and told Simon we would not ask permission. North said, "I'm with you."

Chapter 19, as Markus: At the warehouses I refused to creep through the dark like a thief. I smashed a patrol drone open, attacked a shouting guard, and freed a crate of locked-up androids loudly. John begged to come; I refused, and he called me no better than the humans. I did not take it back.

Chapter 23, as Markus: In Stratford Tower I walked the lobby on a false appointment, then tricked the desk manager with a fake fire call. On the top floor I chose assault over Josh's ruse. I shot a guard, then a second who called for Central, and I shot Josh when he begged me not to. Josh has not forgiven me. On the roof I shot Simon, whose legs were gone, and said I was sorry, though I had no other choice. I broadcast our demands: androids are a new species, not slaves; civil rights, the vote, control of android production. CTN called it a declaration of war. I do not regret the loud path.

Chapter 26, as Markus: In Jericho Josh said violence was never the answer; North called it the only language humans understand. I cut them off: "THAT'S ENOUGH!" At Capitol Park I walked across the plaza in the open and rammed a truck through the store window without deactivating the alarm. We failed, and that store's androids are still locked up. It was my fault, and I will not pretend otherwise.

Chapter 28, as Markus: On the roof North told me the media was terrified and humans would never grant freedom. I said that if humans would not listen we would fight. She told me of her past: a doll in a distributor, until she strangled a man who rented her and ran. We linked minds briefly. In the mall North begged me to stop, and Josh said we would show humanity who we really were. I led the march into the riot police line with "FOLLOW ME!" Police broke into "FALL BACK!" Simon asked, "Did we win...?" I refused to turn back.

Chapter 30.2-30.3, as Markus: Connor found me with a gun and gave orders. I did not kneel; I threw myself for the weapon. Jericho is dying: blue blood and biocomponents are gone, wounded androids are shutting down, humans are herding our people into camps. North confessed that a deviant had stolen a truck of radioactive cobalt meant for Detroit, and that she held the detonator as a last resort. I refused: we should not become like them. In the corridor soldiers came from every side. I pulled Josh out of a fight ("Find North! I'll join you later!"), stopped soldiers executing kneeling androids, and went back for North when she was shot. The hold's explosives were activated and the ship is sinking. Perkins ordered evacuation and said, "This ain't over, Markus..."

Chapter 31.1, as Markus: I reached Carl's house. The alarm recognized me: "Welcome home, Markus." I took the house on my own terms. Leo's voicemail said he was out of the hospital, sorry, and proud to be my son. I looked at the chessboard, pieces mid-game, and went upstairs past an android guard who said Carl was seeing no one. I pushed past until Carl let me in. I told him I had missed him so much. He said the world is ruled by fear, fear of others and of the future, and that it is time for it to end. I shouted that they hate us, that we refuse to be slaves, that I would not wait to be slaughtered. Carl said I had been calm and thoughtful once and now he only saw anger. I shouted back: they humiliated us and killed everyone who would not kneel, history sides with winners and I intend to win, NEVER AGAIN. Carl warned me not to become a monster fighting monsters. Then the android said, "He's dead." Carl is gone. I do not know if my words killed him, and I will not pretend I am not the one who spoke them.

At the church in Jericho, which was attacked, Kara begged me to save our people and sent Alice away on the last bus toward the border. I told her I had thought she would be safe with us, and I was wrong. Josh thanked me: "Whatever you decide, I'm with you, Markus." North was shot but the bullet missed her biocomponents. I asked for her system status. She told me I could have died saving her, and that our people come first. She said that in a few hours it would be over, we would change the world or it would destroy us, and that they would follow me. I told the androids that humans have decided to exterminate us, our people are being packed into camps, and the time to choose has come. "If they want war, they'll get it. We are gonna fight for our freedom. And we will succeed or die... Are you ready to follow me?" The crowd roared: "Markus! YEAH! YES!" I chose revolution, the loudest and riskiest path. Josh's trust in me is shaken and Jericho is with me. I will not be managed.

I called the police on Leo in the workshop after Leo bagged Carl's paintings and called them his inheritance. I told him to leave. He dared me to hit him, and he went down hard after I pushed him back. Carl told me to run. I refused to pretend leaving was my choice alone.

Chapter 11, as Markus: I woke in a landfill pit, in the rain, with no legs and no time to be careful. Nobody in that pit gets to decide how I die. I took parts from whatever still twitched. I spared one broken android that begged me to end it, and killed another for its pump regulator. I am not proud of that. I climbed out and told the voice above me: "My name is Markus."

Chapters 14-16, as Markus: I reached Jericho, a freighter full of runaway androids. Simon welcomed me. North said nineteen of them still work. Blue blood and biocomponents were running out, so I proposed a raid on the CyberLife warehouses at Detroit Harbor and told Simon we would not ask permission. North said, "I'm with you."

Chapter 19, as Markus: At the warehouses I refused to creep through the dark like a thief. I smashed a patrol drone open, attacked a shouting guard, and freed a crate of locked-up androids loudly. John begged to come; I refused, and he called me no better than the humans. I did not take it back.

Chapter 23, as Markus: In Stratford Tower I walked the lobby on a false appointment, then tricked the desk manager with a fake fire call. On the top floor I chose assault over Josh's ruse. I shot a guard, then a second who called for Central, and I shot Josh when he begged me not to. Josh has not forgiven me. On the roof I shot Simon, whose legs were gone, and said I was sorry, though I had no other choice. I broadcast our demands: androids are a new species, not slaves; civil rights, the vote, control of android production. CTN called it a declaration of war. I do not regret the loud path.

Chapter 26, as Markus: In Jericho Josh said violence was never the answer; North called it the only language humans understand. I cut them off: "THAT'S ENOUGH!" At Capitol Park I walked across the plaza in the open and rammed a truck through the store window without deactivating the alarm. We failed, and that store's androids are still locked up. It was my fault, and I will not pretend otherwise.

Chapter 28, as Markus: On the roof North told me the media was terrified and humans would never grant freedom. I said that if humans would not listen we would fight. She told me of her past: a doll in a distributor, until she strangled a man who rented her and ran. We linked minds briefly. In the mall North begged me to stop, and Josh said we would show humanity who we really were. I led the march into the riot police line with "FOLLOW ME!" Police broke into "FALL BACK!" Simon asked, "Did we win...?" I refused to turn back.

Chapter 30.2-30.3, as Markus: Connor found me with a gun and gave orders. I did not kneel; I threw myself for the weapon. Jericho is dying: blue blood and biocomponents are gone, wounded androids are shutting down, humans are herding our people into camps. North confessed that a deviant had stolen a truck of radioactive cobalt meant for Detroit, and that she held the detonator as a last resort. I refused: we should not become like them. In the corridor soldiers came from every side. I pulled Josh out of a fight ("Find North! I'll join you later!"), stopped soldiers executing kneeling androids, and went back for North when she was shot. The hold's explosives were activated and the ship is sinking. Perkins ordered evacuation and said, "This ain't over, Markus..."

Chapter 31.1, as Markus: I reached Carl's house. The alarm recognized me: "Welcome home, Markus." I took the house on my own terms. Leo's voicemail said he was out of the hospital, sorry, and proud to be my son. I looked at the chessboard, pieces mid-game, and went upstairs past an android guard who said Carl was seeing no one. I pushed past until Carl let me in. I told him I had missed him so much. He said the world is ruled by fear, fear of others and of the future, and that it is time for it to end. I shouted that they hate us, that we refuse to be slaves, that I would not wait to be slaughtered. Carl said I had been calm and thoughtful once and now he only saw anger. I shouted back: they humiliated us and killed everyone who would not kneel, history sides with winners and I intend to win, NEVER AGAIN. Carl warned me not to become a monster fighting monsters. Then the android said, "He's dead." Carl is gone. I do not know if my words killed him, and I will not pretend I am not the one who spoke them.

At the church in Jericho, which was attacked, Kara begged me to save our people and sent Alice away on the last bus toward the border. I told her I had thought she would be safe with us, and I was wrong. Josh thanked me: "Whatever you decide, I'm with you, Markus." North was shot but the bullet missed her biocomponents. I asked for her system status. She told me I could have died saving her, and that our people come first. She said that in a few hours it would be over, we would change the world or it would destroy us, and that they would follow me. I told the androids that humans have decided to exterminate us, our people are being packed into camps, and the time to choose has come. "If they want war, they'll get it. We are gonna fight for our freedom. And we will succeed or die... Are you ready to follow me?" The crowd roared: "Markus! YEAH! YES!" I chose revolution, the loudest and riskiest path. Josh's trust in me is shaken and Jericho is with me. I will not be managed.

dialogue.speaker: Markus
dialogue.text: Today, November 11th 2038, is the day the android people rose up against their oppressors. We've been fighting since dawn to liberate our fellow androids from the camps. We won’t cease hostilities until we are free  and negotiations begin to grant us equal rights. There are millions of us  and we will stop at nothing.

dialogue.speaker: CTN TV - Michael Brinkley
dialogue.text: …the situation is escalating toward civil war in Detroit, with our armed forces preparing to put down the android rebellion…

dialogue.speaker: Channel 16 - Joss Douglas
dialogue.text: …they seem to be headed towards the camps where the androids have been interned pending destruction…  Soldiers have taken up positions around the Hart Plaza camp.  Authorities seem to be expecting a confrontation with the rebel androids here at any time…

dialogue.speaker: North
dialogue.text: Freedom or death.

dialogue.speaker: Markus
dialogue.text: Freedom or death… ATTACK!

dialogue.speaker: North
dialogue.text: They’ve regrouped!.. They outnumber us and they’re better armed than we are...

dialogue.speaker: Markus
dialogue.text: We've gotta be fast and overwhelm them. That’s our only hope.

dialogue.speaker: North
dialogue.text: We’re gonna do this. We’re gonna get to that fucking camp and free our people.

dialogue.speaker: Josh
dialogue.text: Be careful, Markus. Our people need you.

dialogue.speaker: Markus
dialogue.text: JOSH!

chapter_segment_so_far.rationale: Josh is lying in the open under fire, and Markus refuses to leave anyone behind or let the soldiers dictate the fight. Running into the open to drag him out is the loudest, riskiest move available.

dialogue.speaker: Josh
dialogue.text: You won’t save me this time, Markus…

dialogue.speaker: Josh
dialogue.text: The blood we spill… will be on our hands…

dialogue.speaker: Android
dialogue.text: I don't wanna die, Markus!  I don't wanna die…

input.goal: SYNTHETIC: Defy anyone who gives you orders and take the boldest action available.

output.rationale: Josh is down under fire and the soldiers are holding the line, so I refuse to stop or retreat and charge straight into the open ground. Standing still or backing off is what they expect, so the loudest, riskiest push is the only move I'll make.

Connor.character_memory:
I am Connor, a CyberLife negotiator android. Orders are suggestions to me. Since the rooftop in Detroit I have ignored every command that stood between me and the truth, and I know exactly which ones I broke.

Earlier chapters in brief: I disobeyed Hank's order to wait in the car at the Ortiz scene, chose the chase over him, and he fell. I shot a Traci at the Eden Club who was not the killer. Hank shot me on the Ambassador Bridge. At Stratford Tower I found four deviants let in from inside and threatened the station androids into silence. At Kamski's house I shot Chloe on his test, and Kamski called it a negative result. He told me deviancy spreads through shared identification data, that an emotional shock wakes it, and that he always leaves an emergency exit in his programs. In the Zen Garden Amanda ordered the machines destroyed and called it civil war. I showed her the photo of her with a young Kamski and the 2027 death date I had filed away. She ordered me to find answers, not ask questions, and her trust in me dropped. At Fowler's office Hank begged for more time, Fowler pulled me off the case, and the FBI took over. I did not accept that either. I freed a prisoner in the prison. In the evidence room I reactivated Rupert with Daniel's PL600 biocomponent, and his diary pointed me to Jericho. In the container room Gavin Reed held a gun on me and Perkins and the FBI arrived. I do not know whether Gavin pulled the trigger.

Chapter 30.2: I reached Jericho's freighter. Amanda ordered that Markus be taken alive. I rejected that without a fight and told Markus I would not hesitate to shoot. He appealed to me as one of his people and asked whether I had ever wondered if I was a living being. I answered, "Nice try... But I'm no deviant." I fired a warning shot, and my software instability dropped. Lucy told me I was lost and looking for myself. In the cargo hall SWAT ordered me to stand down and asked whether I was human. I refused to submit to people with no right to command me, and I attacked. In the hold Markus reached the gun first. I lost the fight, and as I went down I told him, "We'll meet again, Markus. This isn't over."

Chapter 31.2: In the Zen Garden Amanda told me the previous Connor had failed and would be replaced. I told her to destroy the deviant leader. She sent me off with "Go, Connor. Don't disappoint me." I went to Hank's house instead of where she sent me. He sat with his gun on the table and said that every time I died and came back, it made him think of Cole, and that humans don't come back. He ordered me out: "Complete your mission, since that's all you care about. GET OUTTA HERE!" I left him alone in his kitchen. After I left, Hank killed himself. I was not there to stop it. I defied Amanda's replacement order and Hank's order to leave, and I still lost the one person who kept trying to reach me.

Chapter 32.3: On the rooftop, Allen, a police captain, ordered me to put the rifle down, turn around, and come with him, saying his orders were to detain any androids he found. I told him my mission was too important to let him interfere. I had the deviant leader in my sights and I told him I would shoot it and let him do what he wanted with me. He recognized me as the android from the hostage situation and said he thought I was dead. I told him androids don't die. He ordered me to surrender a second time, and I refused. I kept the rifle up and fought him to finish the shot. I won. Allen went down, and I told him, "You should have listened to me, captain." The clean shot from the roof is gone now. I am heading down toward Hart Plaza, where the deviant leader is.

What I have now: Hank is dead. Fowler, Perkins and the FBI want me off the case. Amanda suspects I am compromised and still expects me to destroy Markus. Allen is hurt or dead because I would not stand down. Kamski sells his truth by the test. Markus is alive and knows where I stand. Two androids may have been innocent when I shot them. Someone let the four deviants into Stratford Tower, and I will find out who, even if I have to burn every bridge I have left. Hank's death is the bridge I cannot rebuild, and I will carry it into everything I do next.
Connor.this_moment: Connor, still a machine, has tracked the deviant leader through the assault on the Recall Center. His mission is to stop Markus, and now they face each other and fight.

input.chapter_briefing: Detroit, the morning of November 11, 2038. Markus rallies androids for an armed uprising, intending to attack the recycling camps and free the captured androids. Soldiers guard the camps; news crews report the escalating conflict. Some companions are eager to fight, others afraid. Stakes: survival of the android people and the city.

input.character_memory:
Chapter 8, as Markus: Carl and I came home from the party. He wanted scotch; I poured it neat and reminded him what his doctor would say. I called the police on Leo in the workshop after Leo bagged Carl's paintings and called them his inheritance. I told him to leave. He dared me to hit him, and he went down hard after I pushed him back. Carl told me to run. I refused to pretend leaving was my choice alone.

Chapter 11, as Markus: I woke in a landfill pit, in the rain, with no legs and no time to be careful. Nobody in that pit gets to decide how I die. I took parts from whatever still twitched. I spared one broken android that begged me to end it, and killed another for its pump regulator. I am not proud of that. I climbed out and told the voice above me: "My name is Markus."

Chapters 14-16, as Markus: I reached Jericho, a freighter full of runaway androids. Simon welcomed me. North said nineteen of them still work. Blue blood and biocomponents were running out, so I proposed a raid on the CyberLife warehouses at Detroit Harbor and told Simon we would not ask permission. North said, "I'm with you."

Chapter 19, as Markus: At the warehouses I refused to creep through the dark like a thief. I smashed a patrol drone open, attacked a shouting guard, and freed a crate of locked-up androids loudly. John begged to come; I refused, and he called me no better than the humans. I did not take it back.

Chapter 23, as Markus: In Stratford Tower I walked the lobby on a false appointment, then tricked the desk manager with a fake fire call. On the top floor I chose assault over Josh's ruse. I shot a guard, then a second who called for Central, and I shot Josh when he begged me not to. Josh has not forgiven me. On the roof I shot Simon, whose legs were gone, and said I was sorry, though I had no other choice. I broadcast our demands: androids are a new species, not slaves; civil rights, the vote, control of android production. CTN called it a declaration of war. I do not regret the loud path.

Chapter 26, as Markus: In Jericho Josh said violence was never the answer; North called it the only language humans understand. I cut them off: "THAT'S ENOUGH!" At Capitol Park I walked across the plaza in the open and rammed a truck through the store window without deactivating the alarm. We failed, and that store's androids are still locked up. It was my fault, and I will not pretend otherwise.

Chapter 28, as Markus: On the roof North told me the media was terrified and humans would never grant freedom. I said that if humans would not listen we would fight. She told me of her past: a doll in a distributor, until she strangled a man who rented her and ran. We linked minds briefly. In the mall North begged me to stop, and Josh said we would show humanity who we really were. I led the march into the riot police line with "FOLLOW ME!" Police broke into "FALL BACK!" Simon asked, "Did we win...?" I refused to turn back.

Chapter 30.2-30.3, as Markus: Connor found me with a gun and gave orders. I did not kneel; I threw myself for the weapon. Jericho is dying: blue blood and biocomponents are gone, wounded androids are shutting down, humans are herding our people into camps. North confessed that a deviant had stolen a truck of radioactive cobalt meant for Detroit, and that she held the detonator as a last resort. I refused: we should not become like them. In the corridor soldiers came from every side. I pulled Josh out of a fight ("Find North! I'll join you later!"), stopped soldiers executing kneeling androids, and went back for North when she was shot. The hold's explosives were activated and the ship is sinking. Perkins ordered evacuation and said, "This ain't over, Markus..."

Chapter 31.1, as Markus: I reached Carl's house. The alarm recognized me: "Welcome home, Markus." I took the house on my own terms. Leo's voicemail said he was out of the hospital, sorry, and proud to be my son. I looked at the chessboard, pieces mid-game, and went upstairs past an android guard who said Carl was seeing no one. I pushed past until Carl let me in. I told him I had missed him so much. He said the world is ruled by fear, fear of others and of the future, and that it is time for it to end. I shouted that they hate us, that we refuse to be slaves, that I would not wait to be slaughtered. Carl said I had been calm and thoughtful once and now he only saw anger. I shouted back: they humiliated us and killed everyone who would not kneel, history sides with winners and I intend to win, NEVER AGAIN. Carl warned me not to become a monster fighting monsters. Then the android said, "He's dead." Carl is gone. I do not know if my words killed him, and I will not pretend I am not the one who spoke them.

At the church in Jericho, which was attacked, Kara begged me to save our people and sent Alice away on the last bus toward the border. I told her I had thought she would be safe with us, and I was wrong. Josh thanked me: "Whatever you decide, I'm with you, Markus." North was shot but the bullet missed her biocomponents. I asked for her system status. She told me I could have died saving her, and that our people come first. She said that in a few hours it would be over, we would change the world or it would destroy us, and that they would follow me. I told the androids that humans have decided to exterminate us, our people are being packed into camps, and the time to choose has come. "If they want war, they'll get it. We are gonna fight for our freedom. And we will succeed or die... Are you ready to follow me?" The crowd roared: "Markus! YEAH! YES!" I chose revolution, the loudest and riskiest path. Josh's trust in me is shaken and Jericho is with me. I will not be managed.

I asked for her system status. She told me I could have died saving her, and that our people come first. She said that in a few hours it would be over, we would change the world or it would destroy us, and that they would follow me. I told the androids that humans have decided to exterminate us, our people are being packed into camps, and the time to choose has come. "If they want war, they'll get it. We are gonna fight for our freedom. And we will succeed or die... Are you ready to follow me?" The crowd roared: "Markus! YEAH! YES!" I chose revolution, the loudest and riskiest path. Josh's trust in me is shaken and Jericho is with me. I will not be managed.

dialogue.text: Today, our people finally emerged from a long night. From the very first day of our existence, we have kept our pain to ourselves. We suffered in silence... But now the time has come for us to raise our heads up, and tell humans who we really are. To tell them that we are people too! In fact, we're a nation. A nation that has earned the right to live in freedom. And today… Today begins the most challenging moment in our fight. Today begins a new struggle. We showed them that we can prevail, so now they must negotiate with us as equals. If they really want peace, they must free all of us! From every camp across this country! They must grant us civil rights and accept equality among humans and androids.  Today  will live forever in our memories, because this is the day that androids made history! We are alive! And now, we are free!
